sections.h2: Where is Batavia, and how does it compare with its neighbors?
sections.html:
Batavia sits along the Fox River in the western Chicago suburbs, mostly in Kane County with a part in DuPage. Together with St. Charles and Geneva it forms the Tri-City area, three suburbs of similar size and means.

The 2020 census counted 26,098 residents, and the July 2025 Census estimate is 26,586, 0.3% above the 2020 base. Land area is 10.62 square miles, a density of 2,458 residents per square mile in 2020.

sections.h2: Why is Batavia called the Windmill City?
sections.html:
Settlers arrived in 1833, which makes Batavia the oldest city in Kane County. People first called the place Big Woods, until a local judge gave it the name of his old home, Batavia, New York, in 1840. Incorporation followed on July 27, 1872.

Six American-style windmill manufacturers operated here before 1900, and through the early 1900s three of them turned out most of the windmill-driven water pumps on American farms. Many of the limestone factory buildings still stand and now serve as government and commercial offices and storefronts. The Aurora Elgin and Chicago Railway built a power plant in southern Batavia and added a branch to the city in 1902, and the Campana factory, built in 1936 to make cosmetics including Italian Balm, is another landmark.

The river and the factory district shaped the oldest part of town, so a Batavia price starts with the block.

sections.h2: What jobs and employers shape Batavia's housing market?
sections.html:
Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory, a federal high-energy physics laboratory where the bottom and top quarks were first detected, sits just east of the city limits, and many residents work there. Aldi, Inc., the U.S. subsidiary of Aldi Süd, has its headquarters in Batavia.

The 2022 Economic Census lists $466.2 million in retail sales in the city, $120.5 million in transportation and warehousing, and $108.6 million from health care and social services. Close to 69% of residents 16 or older work or seek work, and the mean commute is 28.9 minutes. The Census Bureau lists 5.8% of residents as foreign-born.

sections.h2: How is Batavia governed, and which schools serve it?
sections.html:
The city council has 14 members. Seven wards each elect two aldermen, and the mayor chairs the council and is elected citywide every four years.

  • Batavia Public School District 101 has six K-5 elementary schools, one 6-8 middle school and Batavia High School.
  • Small pockets of the city belong to Geneva Community Unit School District 304 and to West Aurora District 129.
  • The Batavia Public Library District, founded in April 1881 as a township library, serves most of Batavia Township and parts of nearby townships, and its current building opened in January 2002.

Because the district line can follow a street instead of a city boundary, confirm the school assignment for your address before you repeat a school claim in a listing.

sections.h2: What are the main roads and transit options in Batavia?
sections.html:
Batavia Avenue is Illinois Route 31, Main Street is Route 10 and Washington and River streets carry Illinois Route 25 along the river. Randall Road and Wilson Street are also major streets.

Pace operates some bus service, and the Geneva and Aurora Metra stations are nearby. Paths for biking and walking run along the Fox River. Two railroad lines, the Chicago & North Western Aurora Branch and the Burlington Route West Chicago line, served the city directly until 1943, and today a buyer who commutes by train will ask how far the house is from the nearest platform.

  • Check your house's distance to Route 31 or Randall Road, since buyers weigh traffic and access.
  • Mention river-path access if it is within walking distance.

sections.h2: Which county handles my deed and property record in Batavia?
sections.html:
Most of the city is in Kane County, whose offices are at 719 Batavia Avenue, Building A, in Geneva, open weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30 with some offices keeping other hours. A portion of Batavia is in DuPage County, so check the parcel number on your tax bill to see which recorder and treasurer apply.

Illinois transfer tax is paid with stamps the recorder sells, per the Department of Revenue, and both parties sign Form PTAX-203 for the county. Home rule municipalities may levy extra, so ask the title company whether Batavia does. For recording charges, contact your county's recorder.

sections.h2: What do the Fox River and downtown offer a Batavia seller?
sections.html:
Paths for walking and biking run along the Fox River, and several of the old limestone windmill factories now hold government offices, shops and other businesses. The Batavia Public Library District began in April 1881 as a township library and has been in its present building since January 2002. It serves most of Batavia Township and parts of Winfield, Geneva and Blackberry townships.

If your house is within walking distance of the river or the old factory district, say so in the first line of the description. If it sits closer to Randall Road, lead with the road access instead.

sections.h2: Who lives in Batavia, and what does that mean for resale?
sections.html:
The 2020 census recorded 9,970 households. Children under 18 lived in 34.0% of them, and one person lived alone in 24.8%. Residents had a median age of 41.6, and 17.1% were 65 or older. Vacancy touched 4.0% of the 10,381 housing units, with rates of 0.9% for owned homes and 6.2% for rentals.

Residents tend to stay put, with 91.3% of people aged one and over in the same home a year earlier. Buyers weighing a Batavia address are comparing it with Geneva and St. Charles, the two other Tri-City suburbs, so price against all three.

sections.h2: When does selling a Batavia house for cash make sense?
sections.html:
Selling for cash as-is fits a house with tired systems, a property from an estate, or an owner with a fixed moving date. A listing fits a house in show-ready shape.

  • Ask for the offer in writing and set it beside the net from a listing after repairs and fees.
  • Confirm how quickly the buyer can close and who covers title and recording.
  • Gather your tax bill, payoff letter and permit records before the title company asks.

Whichever way you sell, the paperwork looks the same. The deed has to name every owner, any lender must be paid off from the proceeds, and the recorder in the parcel's county files the transfer. Batavia sits in both Kane and DuPage counties, so a parcel in the DuPage portion follows a different office than one in the Kane portion. Gather the closing documents early, and ask for a copy of the recorded deed once the county returns it.

faqs.q: Is my Batavia house in Kane or DuPage County?
faqs.a: Most likely Kane, though part of the city lies in DuPage. The parcel number on your tax bill settles it and tells you which recorder files the deed.
Batavia Public School District 101 covers most of the city, with small areas in Geneva District 304 and West Aurora District 129. Check your address.
The Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, completed by buyer and seller and filed in the county of the parcel as part of the recording.

faqs.q: Do I have to repair before a sale?
faqs.a: No. Plenty of buyers take houses in their current state, and a cash offer reflects the condition. Insist on written terms and weigh the net against a listing.
The sale contract decides. Revenue stamps for the state tax come through the county recorder, and a home rule municipality or county may add its own. Your title company can list each charge.
